title: Extract shared bash lib to dedupe skill score/scan scripts
description:
9 skills each carry their own scripts/score-*.sh or scan-*.sh (release-readiness/scripts/scan-release.sh,
repo-hygiene/scripts/repo_hygiene.sh, plan-review/scripts/scan-headers.sh + score-plan.sh,
spec-review/scripts/score-spec.sh, diff-review/scripts/collect-diff.sh,
plan-author/scripts/score-draft.sh, api-design-review/scripts/scan-api.sh,
test-plan-review/scripts/scan-tests.sh, readme-review/scripts/score-readme.sh). Each
independently reimplements: markdown frontmatter parsing, markdown section/header scanning,
and percent/color terminal output formatting.

Add a shared lib/common.sh at repo root with the deduplicated versions of these three
utilities, and refactor the 9 scripts above to source it (`source
"$(dirname "$0")/../../lib/common.sh"` or equivalent relative path) instead of reimplementing.
Keep each script's actual scoring logic (the part specific to that skill) untouched — this is
a pure extraction, not a behavior change. Run each refactored script against its existing
sample/fixture input (where one exists, e.g. plan-review's SELF-TEST.md sample) before/after
to confirm output is byte-identical.

Related: ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md (follow-on work list).

title: Add server-side skills-validate Argo WorkflowTemplate (ADR-1 decision part b)

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md (Status: Accepted) states the static validation harness is wired in TWO places: (a) a local git pre-commit hook, and (b) 'a new minimal Argo WorkflowTemplate (skills-validate, added to declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/) triggered on push to this repo, so the check also runs server-side for contributions that bypass the local hook.' Existing bead jcs-5rq covers only the validate-skills.sh script + install-hooks.sh local hook (part a). Part (b), the server-side WorkflowTemplate, is not tracked by any open bead. Evidence: no workflow/CI manifests exist in this repo (only .beads/config.yaml), and this repo is absent from the Available WorkflowTemplates table.

Scope: define the skills-validate WorkflowTemplate in jedarden/declarative-config under k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/ (that cross-repo change is out of this repo's tree, per ADR-1's own note that server-side enforcement is a separate PR/sync). This bead tracks that follow-through so ADR-1 is not left half-implemented.

Acceptance criteria:
- A WorkflowTemplate named skills-validate exists in declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/ and is synced by ArgoCD (app argo-workflows-ns-iad-ci).
- It clones this repo and runs scripts/validate-skills.sh (from jcs-5rq), failing the workflow on non-zero exit.
- It is triggered on push to jeds-curated-skills (or documented as manually submittable until push-trigger wiring exists), pinned to a specific image digest/tag (never :latest).
- README.md or docs note that server-side validation runs in iad-ci.

Blocked-by (prose, no formal edge added): jcs-5rq must land scripts/validate-skills.sh first.

title: Add root install.sh for selective, non-destructive skill installs
description:
README.md's install instructions are: clone the whole repo directly into ~/.claude/skills/, or
manually `cp -r <skill> ~/.claude/skills/` one at a time. The first option assumes an empty or
absent ~/.claude/skills/ — on this very machine, ~/.claude/skills/ already has 7 skills from
other sources (bd-to-br-migration, beads-overview, claude-status, find-stubs, gap-review,
generate-image, new-repo) plus 2 already installed from this repo (plan-review, repo-hygiene);
cloning this repo directly over that directory would collide/fail.

Add scripts/install.sh (or root install.sh) supporting:
  ./install.sh <skill-name> [<skill-name>...]   # install just these skills
  ./install.sh --all                             # install every skill in this repo
Both modes copy into ~/.claude/skills/<skill>/ without touching any other directory already
there, and print a clear "already installed, overwriting" notice (not a silent clobber) when a
target skill directory already exists. Update README.md's Installation section to lead with
this script instead of the raw `git clone .../.claude/skills` command.

Related: ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md (follow-on work list).

title: Add version field to SKILL.md frontmatter + root CHANGELOG.md
description:
Skills are cp'd once and never re-synced (see the drift-checker bead) — there is currently no
signal to a user with an old local copy that a skill has changed upstream. Add a `version:
X.Y.Z` field to every */SKILL.md frontmatter block (start all 14 at 1.0.0) and a root
CHANGELOG.md following Keep a Changelog format, with one entry per skill covering its history
to date (can be reconstructed from `git log --follow <skill>/`).

Going forward, bump a skill's version and add a CHANGELOG.md entry whenever its SKILL.md,
checklists, or scripts change materially (typo fixes excluded). This is a convention change,
not just one commit — note the convention in README.md's Philosophy section.

Related: ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md (follow-on work list); pairs with the drift-checker bead
(jcs-3) which can eventually report version mismatches, not just file diffs.

title: Implement scripts/validate-skills.sh per ADR-1
description:
Implement the static structural-validation harness decided in ADR-1
(docs/plan/plan.md, 'ADR-1: 2026-07-20 — Add a static structural-validation harness for skill
bundles'). Add scripts/validate-skills.sh at repo root that, for every top-level skill
directory (one with a SKILL.md):

1. Frontmatter schema — SKILL.md has a YAML frontmatter block; `name:` matches the directory
   name; `description` and `allowed-tools` are present and non-empty.
2. Reference integrity — every CHECKLIST-*.md / REPORT-TEMPLATE.md / subagents/*.md /
   scripts/*.sh filename mentioned in SKILL.md resolves to a file that actually exists in that
   skill's directory.
3. Shell syntax — every scripts/*.sh passes `bash -n`; if `shellcheck` is on PATH also run it
   and print (don't fail on) warnings — must degrade gracefully when shellcheck is absent
   (it is not installed on this machine as of 2026-07-20).
4. Executable bit — every scripts/*.sh referenced from a SKILL.md invocation snippet is
   `chmod +x`.

Also add scripts/install-hooks.sh that installs scripts/validate-skills.sh as a git
pre-commit hook (hooks aren't versioned by git, so this is the install step for local repo
checkouts).

Exit non-zero and print a clear per-skill report if any check fails. Reference ADR-1 in the
script's header comment.

title: Add SDLC lifecycle map doc chaining the 14 skills
description:
The 14 skills cover the agent-driven dev lifecycle end to end (spec-review -> plan-author ->
plan-review -> [implement] -> diff-review -> test-plan-review -> api-design-review ->
threat-model -> release-readiness -> postmortem, with adr and readme-review and repo-hygiene
and usage-statusline cutting across), but nothing in the repo states this chain explicitly —
README.md groups them by category (Plan & design / Implement & verify / Ship & operate /
Observe) but doesn't say "run X, then when Y happens run Z."

Add docs/notes/lifecycle.md: a short doc (diagram or ordered list is fine) mapping each SDLC
stage to the skill(s) to invoke at that point, including the two branch points (spec exists vs.
brief only -> spec-review vs. straight to plan-author; greenfield vs. port/improvement/
integration plan types). Link to it from README.md's Philosophy section.

Related: from the same review pass as ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md.

title: Add installed-copy drift checker script
description:
Skills are distributed by `cp -r` into ~/.claude/skills/ (per README.md) with no update or
drift-detection mechanism. Confirmed live on this machine 2026-07-20: the installed
~/.claude/usage-statusline.sh differs from this repo's usage-statusline/scripts/usage-statusline.sh
by one line (installed copy hardcodes `/home/coding` in its commit-scan `find`, repo's current
version generalized to `$HOME`) — silent drift with nobody aware.

Add scripts/check-installed.sh [skill-name...] that, for each named skill (or all skills if
none named), diffs the corresponding directory under ~/.claude/skills/<skill> against this
repo's <skill>/ directory and reports any files that differ or are missing on either side.
Exit non-zero if drift is found. Document usage in README.md under a new "Checking for drift"
section.

Related: ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md (this repo's own drift finding motivated the harness).

title: Add SELF-TEST.md to diff-review and repo-hygiene
description:
Only plan-review/SELF-TEST.md exists among the 14 skills; the other 13 have zero self-test
coverage (manual or automated). Extend the same pattern (trigger-phrase table, skill-structure
validation commands, script smoke test, functional-test invocation + expected-output
description — see plan-review/SELF-TEST.md for the template) to the two skills whose scripts
are most deterministic and easiest to smoke-test without external fixtures:

- diff-review/SELF-TEST.md — smoke-test scripts/collect-diff.sh against this very repo's git
  history (e.g. `collect-diff.sh HEAD~3` inside a scratch clone), plus a functional-test
  invocation against a small synthetic diff.
- repo-hygiene/SELF-TEST.md — smoke-test scripts/repo_hygiene.sh against this repo itself
  (already confirmed clean 2026-07-20: `bash repo-hygiene/scripts/repo_hygiene.sh .` reports
  "Clean — no findings.") and against a scratch repo seeded with one known violation per
  category (committed node_modules/, a >5MB file, a dead .github/workflows/ file) to confirm
  each check actually fires.

Related: ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md (follow-on work list — functional self-tests are explicitly
out of scope for the static harness in ADR-1 and tracked separately here).
